translationRepairs: When the Ming destroyed the Liang princely house and extinguished Dali, they ruled through native chiefs, organizing the region into Pacification Commissioners, Pacification Supervisors, Reassurance Commissioners, principal and deputy native chiefs, native prefectures, and native subprefectures.

When the Ming defeated the Prince of Liang and extinguished Dali, they ruled through native chiefs, organizing the region into Pacification Commissioners, Pacification Supervisors, Reassurance Commissioners, principal and deputy native chiefs, native prefectures, and native subprefectures.
明破梁王 names the titled Prince of Liang as the defeated party; 'destroyed the Liang princely house' impersonalizes 梁王 and diverges from the personal referent already clear in s0004.
In the twenty-first year, they were taken; Shifan killed himself, and Yunnan was fully settled.
In the twenty-first year, they were overcome; Shifan killed himself, and Yunnan was fully settled.
克之 is the military taking/overcoming of the rebel position, not capture of unspecified persons; 'they were taken' misreads the verb, while 'overcome' matches the sense already in the idiomatic field.

Lu Wanzhong, however, was dominated by a Han collaborator, who persuaded him to send three thousand men from Zhenxiong against Dingkun at Ludian; Ortai dispatched Mobile Corps Commander Ha Yuansheng, who routed them;

Lu Wanzhong, however, was controlled by a Han collaborator; he arranged for three thousand troops from Zhenxiong to attack Dingkun at Ludian; Ortai dispatched Mobile Corps Commander Ha Yuansheng, who routed them;
After 制于漢奸, 約鎮雄兵三千攻鼎坤 keeps Lu Wanzhong as the arranger of the levy; the relative clause invents a persuasion sequence and makes the collaborator the agent of sending the troops.
Ortai assembled more than ten thousand regular troops, with native auxiliaries numbering half as many again, and advanced in three columns.
Ortai assembled more than ten thousand regular troops, with native auxiliaries numbering half as many, and advanced in three columns.
土兵半之 means native troops equal to half the regular force; 'half as many again' wrongly yields 150% of the regulars.

In the sixth year Ortai became governor-general of all three provinces. The native subprefecture of Anyufan, the Zhenyuan native prefecture under Diao Huan, the Zhele chief, and the various native chiefs of Weiyuan and Guangnan were impeached and removed one after another.

In the sixth year Ortai became governor-general of all three provinces. An Yufan of the native subprefecture, Diao Huan of the Zhenyuan native prefecture, the Zhele chief, and the various native chiefs of Weiyuan and Guangnan were impeached and removed one after another.
Parallel 土州安於蕃 with 鎮沅土府刁澣 marks 安於蕃 as the personal name of the native-subprefecture holder, not a place-name Anyufan.

In the sixth year Ortai governed all three provinces; the native subprefecture of Anyufan, the native prefecture of Zhenyuan under Diao Huan, the chief official of Zhele, and the various native chiefs of Weiyuan Subprefecture and Guangnan Prefecture were impeached and removed in succession.

In the sixth year Ortai governed all three provinces; An Yufan of the native subprefecture, Diao Huan of the Zhenyuan native prefecture, the chief official of Zhele, and the various native chiefs of Weiyuan Subprefecture and Guangnan Prefecture were impeached and removed in succession.
Same parallel: 安於蕃 is the person holding the native subprefecture, paired with Diao Huan of Zhenyuan, not a place called Anyufan.
The line passed to Yang Rongchang; in the fiftieth year of Qianlong (1785) the office was reclassified as a hereditary ninth-rank native post.
The line passed to Yang Rongchang; in the fiftieth year of Qianlong (1785) the office was reclassified as a hereditary secondary ninth-rank native post.
從九品 is the secondary (从) ninth rank; omitting 從 as plain 'ninth-rank' upgrades the office beyond the Chinese grade.

His great-grandson A Kouyuan had indulged bandits and harmed the people; in the fourth year of Yongzheng (1726) the post was abolished, he was resettled in Jiangxi, and the territory was brought under regular administration.
His great-grandson A Kouyuan had indulged bandits and harmed the people; in the fourth year of Yongzheng (1726) the post was converted to regular administration and he was resettled in Jiangxi.
Chinese has only 改流，安插江西—conversion to regular administration plus resettlement; the idiomatic triads a separate 'abolished' clause not present as 裁/除.
In the fourth year of Kangxi (1665), he joined Wang Lu's rebellion and was put to death. His lands were organized as Kaifua Prefecture under regular magistrates.
In the fourth year of Kangxi (1665), he joined Wang Lu's rebellion and was put to death. His lands were organized as Kaihua Prefecture under regular magistrates.
開化府 romanizes as Kaihua; Kaifua misreads 化 as fua.
In the fourth year of Kangxi, he followed Wang Lu in rebellion and was executed; his territory became Kaifua Prefecture and regular officials were appointed.
In the fourth year of Kangxi, he followed Wang Lu in rebellion and was executed; his territory became Kaihua Prefecture and regular officials were appointed.
Same romanization error in the literal field: 開化府 is Kaihua, not Kaifua.
The Deputy Chief Official of the Chief Official of Wangnong Mountain.
The Deputy Chief Official of Wangnong Mountain.
王弄山長官司副長官 names the deputy chief of the Wangnong Mountain chief-official office; stacking 'Deputy Chief Official of the Chief Official' is redundant mistranslation.
In the fourth year of Kangxi (1665), Shuo joined Lu Changxian's rebellion. Government forces marched against him; Shuo burned himself alive, and his territory was annexed to Kaifua Prefecture.
In the fourth year of Kangxi (1665), Shuo joined Lu Changxian's rebellion. Government forces marched against him; Shuo burned himself alive, and his territory was annexed to Kaihua Prefecture.
Again 開化府 must be Kaihua; Kaifua is an erroneous romanization.
In the fourth year of Kangxi, Shuo rebelled with Lu Changxian; government troops attacked; Shuo burned himself to death; his territory was placed under Kaifua Prefecture.
In the fourth year of Kangxi, Shuo rebelled with Lu Changxian; government troops attacked; Shuo burned himself to death; his territory was placed under Kaihua Prefecture.
Literal field repeats the Kaifua error; 開化府 is Kaihua.
In the fourth year of Kangxi (1665), Rishen's sons Shifan and Shiping joined Ning's Lu Changxian in rebellion. Regional Commander Yan Zhen crushed the uprising.
In the fourth year of Kangxi (1665), the sons of Rifang's younger brother Rishen, Shifan and Shiping, joined Ning's Lu Changxian in rebellion. Regional Commander Yan Zhen crushed the uprising.
Idiomatic English omits 日芳弟, a real kinship error; the proposed string restores that fact but is garden-path awkward, so rephrase as 'the sons of Rifang's younger brother Rishen, Shifan and Shiping'.

In the nineteenth year of Kangxi of the Qing, when Yunnan was recovered, the native Wang Feng was given a false post as Mobile Corps Commander, was met on the Guangxi road, and submitted in allegiance.

In the nineteenth year of Kangxi of the Qing, when Yunnan was recovered, the native Wang Feng was given a false post as Mobile Corps Commander; he went to the Guangxi road and submitted in allegiance.
迎至廣西路投誠 has Wang Feng going to the Guangxi road to submit; 'was met' reverses the agency of 迎至.
A later holder was dismissed for misconduct; the line passed to Shen Zhaoqian.
Later he was dismissed for a crime; the line passed to Shen Zhaoqian.
後以罪黜 continues the silent hereditary-office subject and does not introduce a new unnamed holder; 'A later holder' invents a person the Chinese does not name.
